newsitem.title: USA: Market timing seen as key tool for mutual funds.
newsitem.headline: Market timing seen as key tool for mutual funds.

text.p: Using market timing strategies in mutual fund investing can protect investors from impending bear markets, market timers said Tuesday at a conference here.

At the Society of Asset Allocators and Fund Timers, Inc (SAAFTI) semi-annual conference, investment advisers called fund timing an important risk management tool, especially for the U.S. baby boomer generation.
Unlike traditional buy-and-hold strategies, classic market timing uses only domestic equity mutual funds, plus a money market fund during defensive periods.

Dynamic asset allocators use market timing, but also use multiple asset classes like international equities, bonds and gold. Technical analysis and computer models generally drive market timing decisions, the advisers said.
For baby boomers, market timing could prevent losses to retirement nest eggs should a bear market take hold, said John Sosnowy, chairman of Sosnowy Investment Management Company.

"Most investors out there today have not experienced what I would call a real bear market," Sosnowy said. "So they've been taught by what's been going on in recent years, that you just buy on the dip. But the problem comes in when the dip turns into a bigger dip and how are people going to react then?"
Market timers, however, looked for the sell signals that preceded a bear market and moved their clients "out of harm's way" and avoided 80 percent of a market's drop, Sosnowy said.

"The thing that I fear is that we've got a whole generation here that's never seen a bear market and we're going to get just about to the point where a lot of those people are retired on a fixed income and making withdrawals from their equity portfolio, and boom, the bottom drops out and they'll never be able to recover," Sosnowy said. "

Steve Shellans, editor of MoniResearch Newsletter, which tracks market timers, said almost all of the timers he monitored were out of domestic equity funds by the time of the stock market crash in 1987.

"The high in that cycle was reached in early August 1987 and from there until the beginning of the crash on October 18, there was steady deterioration and of all the market timers we track were out of the market by October 16 except for possibly one or two," Shellans said.
"So if the next bear market comes upon us with at least some warning, then based on the 1987 experience, most market timers will have their clients safely into cash," he added.
Peter Mauthe, SAAFTI president, said a dominant feature of market timing was that it demonstrated its strength in bear markets.

"If the market is going up, whether you're a timer or not is not important because everybody is going up together. It's only when markets go down and you're protected that you begin to understand the benefits of using any type of timing," Mauthe said.
Market timing, Sosnowy added, was the key to saving "baby boomers from bust." He said buy-and-hold mutual fund strategies did not position investors for an impending bear market.
"Market timing is not going to be anyone's solution to (investing) if we never have another bear market," Sosnowy said. "But these cycles are inevitable."
